scope: Shared program-metadata core consumer integration and exact installed/running identity

behaviors.contract: Expanded Python source inspectors track the shared static project-module report's file, route and missing-candidate observations on the metadata worker. Imported-file edits and newly resolvable local imports invalidate the graph even if the entry file and interpreter are unchanged. Stable observations and unrelated sibling build/cache creation do not re-probe the interpreter. A source edit racing publication discards only the module report while retaining its original refresh baseline, script identity and unrelated runtime/package evidence. Visible expanded source inspectors request bounded periodic worker refresh; painting and copying perform no filesystem reads. Process identity and existing stale-reply rejection remain in force. This graph describes on-disk references, never loaded code or whole-application freshness.

Show Info repairs numeric descriptor-launch comm labels from the same captured executable image used by the process snapshot, including retained/deleted images. Headers, Process name rows and shell/Python script recognition use the recovered name. Nonnumeric custom names, genuinely numeric executable names and unreadable images retain the existing naming policy. No argv0/window-title guesses or extra process scan I/O are added; raw kernel names remain in snapshot identity comparisons so a changed/reused process cannot be accepted merely because its recovered display name agrees.

Shell and Python file-script headings use canonical selectable text Script followed by two spaces and the original script filename, with no colon. The Script label is rose-grey InstanceContext colour, while only the name retains independent same/different/unknown captured/current content colouring. Its rendered value aligns with the parent interpreter process's metadata value column (Capabilities), not the nested script's row width. A reliably captured script filename is preferred over a numeric /proc descriptor route, preserving the extension without asserting unrecorded source provenance. Alignment follows actual font metrics, process depth and display scale in both open and closed script states. Copying and dropdown identity remain unchanged; strikethrough conversion preserves positional padding exactly once. Python modules retain Module name: module, and interactive Python, Node, Java and Electron headings keep their existing styles.

Expanding a shell process preserves the interpreter's verified native executable comparison in the outer process header: current is green, outdated is red, unknown/stale is neutral. Its script-name suffix and nested Script heading independently compare retained/current candidate bytes: Same green, Different red, unavailable/error/stale neutral, without proving original launch provenance or a running version. Python file-script suffixes and nested Script fields use the same independent captured/current script-byte comparison without borrowing the Python interpreter's executable status. Exact captured shell identity displays Interpreter: Bash (or the recognized shell); an unknown name cannot borrow argv0 or today's installation. Kind remains Shell script. UTF-8 spans, separator/PID roles, selection/copy and normal/high-DPI rendering are preserved. The display rule grants no new restart/update actions to shell or Python scripts. Node/Java/Electron hosted headers and Pi receipt precedence retain their existing policies. Formatting performs no executable, filesystem or package queries.

Native version workers preserve shared compiled Qt application-version evidence, complete fork suffixes and its visible qualification. Supported bounded Qt/KDE metadata initialization is proven from each exact pinned ELF, not today's source metadata or an arbitrary neighboring UTF-16 string. Retained and installed images remain independent; neither this evidence nor a retained desktop association changes current-image verification. No discovered GUI program is executed for this passive fallback.

Desktop fields may belong to an exact retained running image even when the current installation points to a newer build. Installed and pinned-running association use fresh, bounded shared desktop receipts; they never alter the current installation, launch chain or publication proof. Names, copied/replaced images, hidden or non-application entries and dynamic shell commands cannot establish identity. Fresh metadata replaces stale cached fields; missing installed icons are not guessed from a checkout.

Existing processes use shared generic native/component/desktop discovery, not app-specific frontend fallbacks. Pinned running versions remain separate from replacement disk components; compiled-initializer qualifications survive display adaptation. Exact live desktop routes restore GUI roles for forks and can identify an explicitly inferred upstream package without conferring native ownership/AUR permission. Large Ninja input observations retain original bounds and read-only log enforcement. An inaccessible deleted product library stays an explicit unknown; no application is launched, signalled or restarted by acceptance checks.

An explicitly supplied existing SSH tunnel retains its PID/start/image and command line while metadata reports the SSH client's exact portable product version and ELF build ID separately from the openssh package release and OpenSSL dependency. The provided executable remains PET and its owning explicit Pacman package remains PEP. Per-tool capabilities preserve direct SSH service targets but do not inherit ssh-keygen's JOB role or unrelated package GUI/library roles. Package-managed compilation remains not applicable. Native process and installed-application consumers agree; no tunnel is created, changed or restarted, and only the audited trusted client -V recipe may execute if passive evidence is unavailable.

An existing deleted Codex code-mode host image and the independently inspected disk image retain their own compiled service versions/build IDs through the shared passive decoder. The helper inherits only exact supported Cargo target provenance from its indexed checkout, receives its own product description/CLI role, and does not borrow the parent CLI's release or desktop fields. Missing old generated Cargo inputs remain counted but alone report qualified Unknown compilation evidence, not edited source. No helper, project or version command executes.

Pi's running SDK and extensions hashes compare independently against their own installed hashes. Only running hashes are coloured; matching code stays green when extensions differ, while stale, missing, malformed or untrusted evidence stays neutral. Installed patch verification, comparison checked/reason and coverage remain backend evidence and do not appear as redundant Show Info fields. Runtime identity and installed package metadata remain separate.

Python file-script sections share Bash's aligned Script  filename.py field-heading presentation. The rose-grey Script label is separate from the original UTF-8 filename, whose green/red/neutral colour describes only its own captured/current script comparison, never the native Python executable, installed distribution version or a proven running-loaded version. The outer script-name suffix uses that same independently matched script-byte comparison. A captured filename with its extension is not replaced by the basename of a /proc descriptor route; missing or stale source evidence remains unverified. Parent label/value columns remain aligned when collapsed or expanded at normal and high DPI; continuous selection, copying, original paths and independent collapse state are preserved. Python module sections retain Module name: module without fabricated file paths or file-script comparison styling. Interactive Python, Node, Java and Electron sections retain their existing policies. This presentation adds no metadata probing, execution authority or update/restart actions.

Show Info omits the Source directory row for Python and other hosted scripts/applications, even when a local source root is known. Python's Git source repository, revision and branch rows are also omitted. Source attribution remains available internally for classification, language and build-system discovery; script paths, source-language/build-system results and package/dependency metadata are not removed or duplicated.

The shared passive decoder can recover an exact uv product release from a renamed uv-bin's native initializer without executing it or mistaking uvx's shim for uv. Each pinned image retains its own version and ELF identity. The Python runtime remains UVR, independent of uv's own unresolved installation provenance. Exact Python source metadata supplies its own description and proven CLI role; non-Git local Dev project attribution is retained internally without displaying a Source directory row. Unbound helpers do not inherit nearby project versions, and current files do not establish running versions or source changes since startup.

Package and Root package rows are omitted for source-managed and unmanaged classifications (FRK, DEV, CLO, OPT, USC, UBI and normalized legacy aliases), regardless of an unrelated or upstream package record. Completed native metadata without an actual owner does not show an empty package row; undecided native ownership may show Loading until classified. Hosted npm applications retain actual installed manifest identities, while other scripts require a non-inferred owning package. Separate upstream Pacman/AUR/npm version comparisons, package values, badge colours and retained backend evidence are unchanged.

Uncompiled changes is omitted from installed application, native process and hosted runtime Info for Pacman/AUR-managed packages, interpreted entries and confirmed not-applicable results, including existing dash representations. A captured system-package owner or installation classification suffices even while details are pending. Detailed backend reasons remain intact for diagnostics. Applicable source-build unknown, unavailable, pending, changed and no-newer results retain their values and distinct meaning; other fields' not-applicable explanations are unchanged.

Application and process Info display the shared compact Uncompiled changes summary: observation, unique recorded inputs checked, separately counted newer and missing inputs, and added: unknown for unrecorded new inputs. Backend explanations and example paths stay out of the main row. A complete revalidated zero-newer/zero-missing observation is distinct from full build completeness, with a full-build-unknown suffix when needed; it is not a clean-build claim. Partial validated scans retain their uncertainty and cannot become a successful no-newer observation; invalidated artifacts and failed inspections cannot display false zero counts. Main-row selection and Copy preserve the exact contiguous UTF-8 text. Inspection must preserve response files and must not run project recipes.

Expanded native-process and installed-application metadata both report the exact GNU coreutils cat product banner, preserving independent package versions and ELF build IDs. A current package-owned cat has not-applicable compilation status; an invalidated process identity suppresses running evidence while retaining separately inspected disk metadata. This opt-in system integration starts only its own stdin-blocked cat fixture and bounded --version probes, and always reaps its fixture without modifying a user's process.

Off-PATH native subprocess build status uses independent pinned running/disk identity and fresh exact package image evidence, not parent status or a desktop-name match. Window desktop entries are unverified child candidates until worker-side current-record/static-chain matching proves the exact image; ambiguous, missing, hidden, stale and mismatched records do not identify children. Window-only metadata and icon fallback do not leak to helpers. Verified package-managed native installations report compilation status not applicable.

Package-version loading text describes checking an available version rather than refreshing databases. Shared package availability coalesces identical active queries without completed-result or disk response caching; each popup retains only its explicitly captured metadata snapshot, and a new lookup can perform a fresh AUR request.

Unresolved same-named source wrappers never replace the exact native image. Running and disk versions/build IDs remain available and stale cached CLI classification yields to exact immutable product metadata. A captured absolute argv0 that remains unchanged and resolves to the independently pinned installed native image verifies the comparison target even outside PATH; matching running builds are green and changed running builds are red in both headers and version fields, including unchanged version text. Retained images without that evidence, rewritten or relative argv0 and changed process identities remain unknown. The GUI and daemon publish independent passive product records in their optimized ELF images; discovered wrappers are never executed.

Expanded process and installed-application queries use shared explicit local grants when passive evidence is unavailable. Local results bypass the main-only inner cache so grants/revocations are reread on worker queries. Inventory discovery and inferred argv0 metadata remain passive. The pinned deleted running Fish version and the separately pinned current installation retain their own versions, build IDs and process identity without restarting the shell.

The generic opt-in process acceptance consumes an independently captured exact PID/start identity, product, running/current physical paths, version reports and full ELF build IDs. A freshly verified indexed local source installation plus protected exact producer evidence permits only an audited historical-safe query of the pinned older image. Running and current installation observations remain distinct through the Launcher adapter; current metadata cannot substitute for missing running evidence. The process identity and both physical image observations remain unchanged. The test never writes grants, inventory, permissions, source/build records or application files, and never rebuilds or restarts the selected application.

CopyQ's complete Qt-object version and Mousepad's private-library version come from the shared passive reader, not executing GUI applications or borrowing source/package versions. Running Mousepad libraries require independent process-mapping proof, installed tiles use disk context, and neither a shared main image nor its build ID proves required components current. Component queries bypass the main-only inner cache and cannot reuse on-disk results as process evidence.
Native product versions/build IDs and launch resolution use program-metadata; unknown or misleading names never authorize execution of user programs
Installed Node and Python payload metadata is distinct from interpreter metadata; unresolved runtime launches remain Unknown and Python/Java installed versions do not claim running-loaded versions

Build freshness delegates to the shared exact-artifact passive query plan; it does not execute project recipes or mutate response files, and unsupported/source-only inference cannot prove a clean build

Verified Open Info metadata is captured once and does not expire on a render timer; observed process executable path or identity changes still invalidate it, stale generations and revisions are rejected, Pi receipt updates stay separate and network queries do not block binary details. Only unverified on-disk candidates have a ten-second bounded background refresh. Process snapshots themselves are captured when Show Info opens, not continuously monitored.
Shared installation labels and package freshness preserve their own evidence; inferred upstream names never authorize AUR queries and running/installed facts stay separate

Renamed/deleted self-updated native images recover their current installation through shared process-context validation, without backup-filename heuristics or mistaking installed metadata for running evidence. Lost process identity cannot authorize recovery and inferred launch routes are identified as such. Recovered interpreters retain their runtime classification without borrowing the replacement's version or authorizing new executable probes.

User-owned tmux versions are extracted passively by program-metadata from the exact pinned ELF function and referenced literal; launcher forwards complete fork versions and independently cached running/installed build identities without executing tmux. The opt-in real-artifact regression requires explicit old/current paths and does not inspect or alter a live server.

Unreadable proc executable/cwd preserve access errors and exact raw argv0; an absolute, live-identity-checked, regular ELF candidate provides only separately labelled passive installed metadata. Display command text, scripts, FIFOs, changed argv0, symlink retargets and stale PID identity cannot authorize a candidate. Candidate refresh and filesystem validation occur on workers, never during painting.

Python's exact version, genuine absence of a GNU build ID, uv runtime provenance and current validated .venv route stay independent. Script source checkout attribution does not invent a running-loaded version, installed distribution version or compilation status, and prebuilt uv runtime compilation status is not applicable.

Native browser freshness accepts a verified current desktop-entry wrapper chain in addition to published binary aliases. Headers and the running Executable Version (ELF build ID) share the verified comparison, while the on-disk version always stays neutral. Unknown, inaccessible, missing/stale desktop, unrelated wrapper and retained-only identities also stay neutral. Collapsed checks remain cached, background-only and free of package lookups.

Show Info combines running Executable Version (ELF build ID) and Latest version on disk (ELF build ID) values as version (ID), without duplicate standalone ELF-ID rows. Process/runtime scopes are preserved and only the running version gets green/red comparison colouring; on-disk versions, missing IDs and installation-only views stay neutral. Diagnostic reasons remain visible and identical loading/unavailable messages are not duplicated. Tmux SHA256 rows follow their corresponding combined version field.

Application and process Show Info colour Uncompiled changes observations and compact checked/newer/missing counts green for No, red for Yes and yellow for Unknown. Only explicit added: unknown, full build status unknown and scan incomplete suffixes are yellow independently of a known observation; no uncertainty text is dropped. Detailed explanations remain backend evidence, while field-label scope colours and original contiguous selected/copied UTF-8 bytes are preserved. Loading, unavailable and not-applicable values stay neutral. Absent desktop entries retain their existing None or pending status without irrelevant icon/name/comment fields; known expected missing paths remain distinct.

behaviors.owner: Shared desktop reader and Applicationlauncher detailed Info workers
behaviors.contract: The existing Desktop file value appends exact current application-target matches with different desktop IDs and all same-ID copies, marking effective/overridden, hidden/unreadable, ambiguous-precedence and same/different/unverified-target states in brackets. Primary metadata and Name/Comment/Icon association stay unchanged; multiple matches do not invent one primary or historical launch provenance. Image stamps and launch routes are revalidated; scripts match their payload rather than their shared interpreter. Search is passive, bounded and cached with detailed metadata, never in rendering/copy/collapsed-header checks. No new field or dropdown is added, full Unicode values remain selectable/copyable, and errors stay in the existing field.

Native process, hosted application/script and installed application Info omit Icon path, Name and Comment unless the captured associated desktop entry has a nonempty desktop file path. Empty-path records and fallback icons cannot create an association. Existing Desktop file None, pending and unavailable/path states and Python's absent-desktop omission remain unchanged. A nonempty associated path retains all desktop fields even when the file is missing or existence/icon/comment metadata is unavailable; association/provenance is not changed and rendering performs no discovery.

Descriptor-backed scripts use the inspected process's pinned file, never the Launcher's same-numbered descriptor. Anonymous/deleted scripts retain their launch identity without invented installed paths or metadata. Process/fd changes invalidate descriptor-derived application fields before publication while preserving independent interpreter evidence. Installed-script refresh follows the guarded target-process fd, notices target sidecars and descriptor reuse, and excludes memfd installations.

behaviors.owner: Shared development artifact readers and installed/hosted language display
behaviors.diagnostic_boundary: Compiler/linker and startup ownership diagnostics do not become language facts or repeat in the component portion of the language line. Application and component failure reasons are typed separately. Expired/unavailable component scans remain explicit Unknowns inline; completed no-evidence component reports are omitted from display rather than shown as None detected. Worker-side exact-artifact reuse revalidates all auxiliary debug routes, including missing-to-present and replacements; unbound aggregate/application facts cannot survive artifact invalidation. No source scan or auxiliary filesystem read is introduced into rendering or copy.
behaviors.contract: One Application languages row places primary/secondary role labels in parentheses after every inspected language, combining rather than losing shared probable, entry-language, binary linked/generated and incomplete qualifiers. Multiple primary languages retain independent confidence; grouped component/entry qualifiers apply to each relevant language, while commas inside nested Unknown reasons remain intact. Unknowns use an explicit primary/secondary role and reason; completed empty secondary results are omitted. Missing/loading metadata remains plain Unknown/Loading until classified evidence exists. Application ownership remains distinct from unowned aggregate component evidence, and established primary language names are excluded from secondary components. Aggregate-only Go/C++ records cannot become application-owned languages. Selected Node entries retain an entry-language qualifier, not an original source claim. The one row preserves installed/retained-script scope and suffix labels in rendered and copied text at normal and 2x DPI, without role prefixes, an empty secondary clause, running-executable fields, a separate Other detected language components row, or freshness colours. Runtime-only observations are explanatory Unknowns, compiler markers never invent a build system, and hosted applications never borrow their interpreter/runtime evidence.
behaviors.host_corpus_acceptance: Ignored cross-boundary tests require explicit absolute PROGRAM_METADATA_TEST_GO_APPLICATION_PATH or PROGRAM_METADATA_TEST_RUST_APPLICATION_PATH to independently established current custom-Go/C++ or source-free Rust/Codex corpus images. Each passively invokes the public shared reader with no checkout and one 750ms deadline, revalidates held-file/path/dependency stamps, and checks typed application ownership before primary UI labels through ProcessVersion, rendered text and egui copy at normal and 2x DPI. Go requires probable ownership plus qualified C++ secondary evidence; Rust components cannot substitute for a proven Rust application entry. Neither test executes an application or queries its version, and ordinary tests do not silently substitute another host binary.

behaviors.owner: Detailed development workers and source-checkout Show Info rows
behaviors.contract: Known FRK/DEV/CLO source checkouts explicitly use the shared source-only checkout reader before executable checks. One source snapshot is read and reused for running/current observations of the selected target even with no accessible executable; distinct targets sharing a checkout cannot borrow each other's facts. Languages and build tools describe the current source checkout, never certify old running/installed image contents, and carry no artifact identity, binary component scan, secondary Unknown, or freshness colour. Source route/dependency observations, not ELF stamps, govern reuse and invalidation. Artifact-only replacement or process/descriptor loss preserves only still-current source snapshots. Existing binary-only public acceptance remains independent with no checkout. Rendering/copy is pure and keeps one Application languages (source checkout) row plus Build system (source checkout) at normal and 2x DPI, including explicit missing/loading states without relabelling stale binary snapshots as source facts.
behaviors.host_corpus_acceptance: The ignored source-only public-to-UI test requires explicit absolute PROGRAM_METADATA_TEST_SOURCE_CHECKOUT and PROGRAM_METADATA_TEST_RUST_APPLICATION_PATH for the real Codex checkout and logical target. It calls only inspect_checkout with the original 750ms aggregate deadline, validates source dependencies, and renders/copies at 1x/2x. It neither opens nor executes the selected executable.

behaviors.contract: Build system (on disk) is omitted for Pacman/AUR-managed applications and runtimes, whether package ownership or classification supplies that identity, even when other development metadata is present. Unmanaged/prebuilt/script entries without configured build steps omit the placeholder too. Source checkouts retain Build system (source checkout), including Unknown/Loading states, and detected non-package build stacks retain their values, order, scope and neutral colours. Hosted applications use their own build evidence and package identity rather than their runtime's. Languages, versions, package comparisons, compilation checks and background discovery are unchanged; rendering and copy do not inspect files.

behaviors.owner: Applicationlauncher metadata workers and Show Info
behaviors.contract: One Application languages row and a separate configured build stack use shared artifact-bound development evidence, explicitly separating application ownership from any inline qualified unowned components using primary/secondary labels after the languages rather than inferring ownership from runtime/dependency presence. Show Info displays on-disk and hosted entry/script language/build facts, not running-executable language/build rows, including in copied text. Loading, unavailable, installed, hosted and retained-script views never add a separate component row. Running native/runtime observations remain independent internally; absent metadata keeps plain Unknown/Loading states, inspected results label each language and omit empty secondary clauses, and original TypeScript is not replaced by the JavaScript runtime. Configured build stacks retain ordered generator/backend identity such as CMake to Ninja versus Make. Only detailed workers inspect evidence, sharing one aggregate deadline; collapsed headers and recurring receipt checks do not scan sources. Exact fresh artifact stamps permit reuse and detect stale same-path entries, process/descriptor invalidation removes only dependent facts, and changed Pi entry routes clear old hosted facts without affecting native versions or freshness colours. Pure formatting and selected/copied long Unicode text retain complete values at normal and high DPI.

Retained-script Info displays captured storage, exact byte size, process fd path, storage target, write/resize seals and SHA-256 alongside explicitly qualified current wrapper candidate route/resolution/hash and content-only comparison. Candidate equality or difference cannot invent original launch provenance, package ownership, a running version or desktop association; ordinary shell scripts omit the unknown Running version and inapplicable Build status rows rather than showing placeholders, including when retained details are missing, errored or stale. Their Kind, content comparison and separate native interpreter version/status remain available; Node/Java/Electron keep their existing unknown Running version and Build status rows. Errors and missing observations stay explicit. Long Unicode paths and full hashes remain selectable/copyable at normal and high-DPI scale; only retained/comparison values carry red/green content comparison colours, never the installed candidate hash. Formatting performs no filesystem work.
